name: Substantia nigra, pars reticulata
summary: The pars reticulata is the ventral, cell-sparse part of the substantia nigra that lies on the crus cerebri and is a dispersed continuation of the internal segment of the globus pallidus. Its GABAergic neurons are an output nucleus of the basal ganglia: they tonically inhibit the superior colliculus, the ventral anterior and mediodorsal thalamus and the pedunculopontine nucleus, and they pause to release saccades, orofacial movements and cognitive actions. It is central to the control of eye movements and to the propagation of seizures, it is disinhibited in parkinsonism and overinhibited in chorea, and it is the reason a nigral lesion affects gaze and axial movement as well as the limbs.

anatomy.location: Ventral substantia nigra spread along the dorsal surface of the crus cerebri from the medial edge near the interpeduncular fossa to the lateral edge of the peduncle, beneath the pars compacta and continuous rostrally with the internal pallidum through the cerebral peduncle.

function: Pars reticulata neurons fire tonically at high rates and hold the superior colliculus, the ventral anterior and mediodorsal thalamus and the brainstem locomotor region under inhibition; striatal direct-pathway neurons inhibit them to release a movement, and subthalamic input excites them to stop one, so they are the final common path of the oculomotor, orofacial and prefrontal basal ganglia loops much as the internal pallidum is for the limbs. Their projection to the superior colliculus gates saccades and their dendrites receive dopamine from the pars compacta, which sets their excitability. Reduced GABAergic output from the nigra to the colliculus underlies the seizure-suppressing effect of nigral inhibition in animal models.

bestView.label: pars reticulata on the dorsal surface of the crus cerebri
ventral substantia nigra above the cerebral peduncle

imaging.normalAppearance: On T2 and susceptibility-weighted images the pars reticulata is the dark, iron-rich band immediately dorsal to the crus cerebri, distinct from the brighter pars compacta behind it; its iron increases in Parkinson disease.

pathology.finding: Increased susceptibility signal in the pars reticulata and loss of the compacta's swallow-tail sign; quantitative susceptibility mapping tracks progression.
Marked hypointensity of the substantia nigra and globus pallidus on T2, with the eye-of-the-tiger sign in PKAN.
Restricted diffusion of the crus and ventral tegmentum with contralateral hemiparesis and parkinsonism, and gaze abnormalities from reticulata involvement.

lesionEffects.deficit: Impaired saccade initiation and slowed eye movements
lesionEffects.mechanism: Loss of reticulata control of the superior colliculus

lesionEffects.deficit: Contribution to parkinsonian akinesia (over-inhibition) or chorea (under-inhibition)
lesionEffects.mechanism: Altered tonic inhibition of the thalamus and brainstem
Loss of nigral gating of the collicular seizure-propagation pathway

examination: Saccade latency and velocity, especially antisaccades
Seizure history in patients with nigral pathology
pearls: The pars reticulata is the pallidum of the eyes and the face
Iron accumulates in the reticulata as dopamine neurons die in the compacta
Nigral output silences the superior colliculus; a saccade is a moment of nigral silence

pitfalls: A dark substantia nigra on T2 is normal in adults; only marked or asymmetric hypointensity with clinical signs suggests iron disease
